subject: Renewal sequencing & retention add-on options
messages:
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>
To: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>, Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 15 Jan 2026 09:32:00 -0800
Subject: Renewal sequencing & retention add-on options

Team —

I pulled together the attached retention cost model and a short checklist (see Drive link) to help us decide sequencing for the Q2 renewals across Datadog / Grafana Cloud / Sentry. High-level asks:

- Confirm contract end dates and any auto-renew windows you own (Hannah, you had a list last quarter).
- Review the cost model assumptions: per-TB storage, egress, compression, and expected growth (attached).
- Legal: flag any change-in-service or audit clauses we should surface early.

Initial thoughts: if Datadog's retention add-on is significantly more expensive per TB than Grafana Cloud's logs tier, we should explore shifting archived logs to Grafana and keeping Datadog for metrics/traces only. That would reduce our Datadog spend but will introduce cross-vendor egress — need architecture and legal input.

Can you each send a 1-paragraph recommendation by EOD Monday? I’ll consolidate and then reach out to vendor reps for updated quotes.

Thanks,
Naomi
Naomi Feldman
Director, Procurement Ops | Redwood Inference
naomi_feldman@redwood.com

Attachments: Retention_cost_model_v2.xlsx, Datadog_current_contract_excerpt.pdf
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>
Cc: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>, Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 15 Jan 2026 11:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Renewal sequencing & retention add-on options

On Thu, Jan 15, 2026 at 09:32 Naomi Feldman wrote:
> Team —
> I pulled together the attached retention cost model...

Quick summary from my side:
- Datadog contract term ends 2026-03-31 (90-day notice window).
- Grafana Cloud term ends 2026-04-30.
- Sentry renewal is 2026-05-15.

Recommendation: prioritize Datadog negotiation first (shortest notice). We should get an updated quote from them that separates ingest vs retention so we can compare apples-to-apples with Grafana. If Datadog /retain-add-on is >40% more /TB than Grafana, push to archive tier in Grafana but get a mock egress estimate.

Also: I’ll pull the usage distribution by service so we can see hot vs cold log ratios.

—Hannah
Hannah Schmitt
Manager, Observability Platform
From: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
Cc: Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 15 Jan 2026 14:22:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Renewal sequencing & retention add-on options

Naomi / team —

Adding a couple of options to consider before we pull vendors into the room: 

1) Consolidate cold retention to Grafana Cloud (cheapest per TB) and keep Datadog for 14–30d hot logs + metrics/traces. Could cut Datadog bill ~25% to 40% but adds cross-vendor restore complexity.
2) Negotiate a blended rate with Datadog for retention if they can match Grafana within X% (we ask for 12 months pricing guarantee).
3) Explore short-term SRE-run compression/retention job to reduce peak ingest while we renegotiate (ops cost vs vendor savings).

Legal / procurement flags: Datadog's MSA has an outbound-data-export clause that can be expensive if egress is charged on their side — we should get explicit egress estimates or a waiver for intra-vendor restores.

I’m available for a 30-min sync tomorrow at 10:00 if that helps.

-Markus
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>
To: procurement@datadog.com
Cc: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>, Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 16 Jan 2026 09:10:00 -0800
Subject: Fwd: Renewal sequencing & retention add-on options — Request for updated quote

Hi Ben / Datadog procurement —

Forwarding our internal thread and an attached retention model. We’re approaching the end of our term on 2026-03-31 and evaluating retention add-on options. Please provide the following by EOD Tuesday:

1) Latest per-TB pricing for log retention tiers (30d, 90d, 365d) and any volume discounts.
2) Explicit egress / restore costs for exporting archived logs to a third-party (per-GB estimate).
3) Any short-term credits or pilot pricing you can offer if we commit to a 12-month retention add-on today.
4) Point person for legal to discuss outbound-data-export and data retention SLA language.

We’ve attached our retention model (expected growth and current usage buckets). If you need a quick sync, Markus is available tomorrow at 10:00 PST.

Thanks,
Naomi

Attachments: Retention_cost_model_v2.xlsx
From: Ben Tyler <ben.tyler@datadog.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@datadog.com
Date: Fri, 16 Jan 2026 17:12:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Fwd: Renewal sequencing & retention add-on options — Request for updated quote

Naomi / team —

Thanks for the details and the model. Quick answers inline: 

1) Per-TB pricing (list price) — 30d: $120 / TB / month; 90d: $85 / TB / month; 365d: $42 / TB / month. We can provide a tiered volume discount above 50 TB / month.
2) Egress/restore — Standard egress at $0.12 / GB; we can offer a one-time discounted restore fee of $0.05 / GB for migrations if committed as part of a renewal.
3) Pilot pricing — We can extend a 3-month trial of the 365d tier at 50% discount if you sign a 12-month retention add-on commitment.
4) Legal contact — cc’d is our commercial counsel (procurement@datadog.com). We can set up a call to walk through the outbound-data-export clause and any waiver options.

Based on your model, if you offload >60% cold logs to Grafana, Datadog savings are modest. Worth a short joint session (Datadog + Grafana) to run a migration cost compare — egress + operational restore tests are likely the gating factor.

I’ve attached a short quote PDF and a sample addendum for outbound exports. Happy to jump on Markus’s slot tomorrow.

Best,
Ben Tyler
Account Executive, Datadog
ben.tyler@datadog.com

Attachments: Datadog_quote_q1_2026.pdf, Datadog_export_addendum_draft.pdf
